That looks quite interesting. ChatGPT's latest update adds a new Mac integration feature: the ability to handle conversation content in Apple's Messages app. This feature supports iMessage, SMS, and RCS.

ChatGPT for Mac now comes with a built-in Apple Messages plugin

The new Apple Messages plugin allows ChatGPT to read and search chat history on Mac, as well as compose and send messages. OpenAI states that this feature is available to all plans of the macOS ChatGPT desktop application, and also supports ChatGPT Work and Codex.

This level of access raises concerns about privacy and control, so OpenAI emphasises that in default settings, sending actions must be authorised by the user. Users should consider carefully before granting permanent authorisation. OpenAI's plugin guidelines detail the associated risks, methods for revoking permissions, as well as a known issue involving tasks that disable authorisation prompts.

Currently, this feature is only available on Mac models equipped with Apple Silicon; Intel models are not supported at this time.

Co-editing websites, shared conversation snapshots, and other features

Although the Messages plugin is the most eye-catching new feature for Apple users, this update also includes many other improvements. For example, pinned conversations are now kept in sync between the ChatGPT desktop app and the iOS version, allowing users to access important conversations at any time across Mac and iPhone.

ChatGPT has also added the ability to share read-only snapshots of Codex local conversations. These snapshots do not change as the original conversation is updated.

Links created with personal accounts can be accessed by anyone with the URL, while workspace links are restricted to members of that workspace. OpenAI states that Codex automatically masks known sensitive formats, but also reminds users to carefully review snapshots, as sensitive information may still remain.

In addition, website owners can invite active members within the same workspace to co-edit websites with collaboration features. After the owner completes the initial publishing, editors can update content and database data, save versions, and publish changes. Owners retain control over access permissions, settings, analytics, and version restoration.

Some website owners can also change the URL hosted by ChatGPT without redeploying, with the old URL automatically redirecting to the new one.

Finally, the Computer History feature launched last week will be expanded to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. This optional feature requires Memories to be enabled and is off by default.
